title: Speed Typer: India Edition
description: Test your typing speed and accuracy with passages about India! Race against the clock to type passages about the diverse beauty of India, the Indian Constitution, and groundbreaking scientific discoveries by Indian scientists. Improve your WPM (words per minute) and accuracy with each attempt.
learning_objectives: Improve typing speed (words per minute) through timed practice
Enhance typing accuracy by minimising errors under pressure
Learn interesting facts about India, its Constitution, and its scientific achievements
Build muscle memory for common English words and sentence patterns
Develop focus and concentration through sustained timed activity

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Choose a passage -- Easy, Medium, or Hard -- based on your confidence level
When the timer starts, type the displayed passage as quickly and accurately as you can
You have 60 seconds to type as much of the passage as possible
Correct characters appear in green; mistakes appear in red so you can self-correct
When the timer ends, review your WPM (words per minute), accuracy percentage, and final score
tips: Focus on accuracy first, speed second -- fixing mistakes costs more time than typing carefully
Keep your eyes on the passage text, not the keyboard -- this builds proper touch-typing habits
Start with the Easy passage to warm up, then challenge yourself with Medium and Hard

passages.title: Incredible India
passages.text: India is a land of incredible diversity. From the snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas in the north to the sun-kissed beaches of Kerala in the south, every region tells a unique story. The country is home to over 1.4 billion people who speak more than 22 officially recognised languages. India gave the world yoga, the number zero, and the game of chess. Its festivals like Diwali, Holi, and Eid bring communities together in celebration.

passages.title: The Indian Constitution
passages.text: The Constitution of India, adopted on 26th November 1949 and enacted on 26th January 1950, is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country in the world. Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, the chairman of the Drafting Committee, is regarded as the chief architect of this remarkable document. The Constitution originally had 395 articles divided into 22 parts and 8 schedules. It establishes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic. The Preamble declares that the people of India resolve to secure justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity for all citizens. Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III protect individuals against arbitrary state action, while Directive Principles in Part IV guide the state in creating policies for social and economic welfare.

passages.title: Indian Scientific Achievements
passages.text: India's contributions to science span millennia, from the ancient mathematician Aryabhata, who calculated the value of pi and proposed that the Earth rotates on its axis, to the modern triumphs of the Indian Space Research Organisation. In 1930, Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman became the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the Raman Effect, which describes how light changes wavelength when scattered by molecules. Decades later, Homi Jehangir Bhabha laid the foundation for India's nuclear programme, establishing the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the Atomic Energy Commission. In 2014, ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission, known as Mangalyaan, made India the first Asian nation to reach Martian orbit, achieving this feat in its very first attempt and at a cost of just Rs 450 crore, less than the budget of many Hollywood films. These achievements demonstrate that scientific excellence transcends economic constraints when driven by ingenuity and determination.

glossary_terms.definition: A standard measure of typing speed. One 'word' is defined as five characters (including spaces). Average typing speed is around 40 WPM; professional typists exceed 80 WPM.
glossary_terms.example: If you type 300 characters in 60 seconds, your WPM is 300 / 5 = 60 WPM.

glossary_terms.definition: A method of typing without looking at the keyboard, relying on muscle memory to find keys. Each finger is assigned specific keys based on the home row position (ASDF for left hand, JKL; for right hand).
glossary_terms.example: Professional writers and coders use touch typing to maintain focus on the screen rather than constantly glancing at the keyboard.

glossary_terms.definition: The percentage of characters typed correctly out of the total characters typed. High accuracy (above 95%) is more important than raw speed because errors require correction time.
glossary_terms.example: Typing 570 correct characters out of 600 total gives an accuracy rate of 95%.

glossary_terms.definition: The introductory statement of the Indian Constitution that outlines the guiding principles and philosophy. It declares India as a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and commits to Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.
glossary_terms.example: The Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India' and was amended by the 42nd Amendment (1976) to include the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular'.

win_conditions.description: Type as much of the passage as possible in 60 seconds! Aim for 40+ WPM with 95%+ accuracy. Score is calculated from WPM multiplied by accuracy -- fast AND accurate typing wins!

transfer_exercises.real_world: Making fast calls during a team project deadline crunch
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice making a decision in under 60 seconds on something you've been procrastinating. Reflect on the outcome.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from mistakes in rapid gameplay
transfer_exercises.real_world: Bouncing back after a failed presentation or test
transfer_exercises.challenge: Write down one recent failure and three specific things you learned from it.

coaching_moment: If you get something wrong, reset and continue. Resilience isn't about never failing — it's about how quickly you get back on track.
cultural_context: India is the world's largest democracy, with a constitution that reflects its extraordinary diversity. Civic literacy and political understanding are essential competencies for India's future citizens and leaders.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did you start to recognize as you played? How will you use it next time?
